text:
The viscera involved (the colon, in irritable bowel syndrome) get their sympathetic innervation from preganglionic neurons in the intermediolateral cell column of the spinal cord at about T10–L2, not L3–L5 as the team note says. Those fibers leave through the lesser and least thoracic splanchnic nerves to the superior mesenteric ganglion for the midgut portion, and through the lumbar splanchnic nerves to the inferior mesenteric ganglion for the hindgut portion. L3–L5 is not a sympathetic outflow level, because the sympathetic outflow is T1–L2. The parasympathetic supply to the distal colon comes from sacral levels S2–S4.

CONFIDENCE: 85
